memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Each of you must respect your mother and father, and you must observe my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God. Do not turn to idols or make metal gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.'" - Lev 19:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the great command to be holy, the first application is: respect your mother and father.

Not a sacrifice. Not a religious ritual. How you treat the two people who raised you.

Notice the order here — mother is named first, which was unusual in the ancient world. And notice how ordinary this is. Holiness begins at home, in the relationships we did not choose and cannot resign from.

That is a searching place to start. It is often easier to be gracious to strangers than to family. We can be patient all day at work and short-tempered within five minutes of walking through our own front door. The people who know us best usually receive the least polished version of us.

Then Sabbath, then idols. Rest and worship — the rhythms that keep a life pointed towards God.

And after each instruction: I am the LORD your God. He signs His name to how you speak to your mother.

If you want to know how your walk with God is going, do not only look at your Bible reading. Look at how you treat the people who share your address.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you treat your family compared to how you treat strangers?
2. Is there a parent you need to honour better, whatever your history?
3. What rhythms of rest and worship keep you pointed towards God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, let my holiness be real where it is hardest — at home, with the people who know me best. Help me honour my parents and keep You at the centre. Amen.
